# Show me

show-me is the habit for the moment a reply would walk through a flow, a hierarchy, a state machine, a comparison or a change to an existing shape, and for the owner asking to be shown, at whatever step the work is in or in a plain answer. Draw a picture where its shape decides something, and of the resulting shape whenever a change moved one, a module extracted or a schema, a state machine or a flow changed, on the turn it lands: prose alone does not show a shape.

## When to draw: the turn and the shape

Find the turn down the side and the shape the reply explains across: the cell is the form to draw, or none. A question about how something works is an explanation, never a plain answer. Draw the part that decides, within twelve nodes and 72 columns.

| The turn | A flow or a sequence | A set of states | A hierarchy | The parts and their joins | A change to a shape | An algorithm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A plain answer | none | none | none | none | none | none |
| A proposal | call tree | box drawing | file tree | component tree | shape diff | pseudocode |
| A build turn that moved code | call tree | box drawing | file tree | component tree | shape diff | pseudocode |
| An explanation | box drawing | box drawing | file tree | component tree | shape diff | pseudocode |
| A close | none | none | none | none | shape diff | none |

## The kinds of lasting visual

| The shape | Inline | The durable kind and its skill | Its permanent home |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a flow, a request's path | a call tree or a box drawing | a sequence diagram, `diagram-design` | a subsystem's journey in the atlas |
| parts and their calls | a component tree or a box drawing | an architecture diagram, `diagram-design` | the map, `architecture-map` |
| a change's shape | a shape diff | the change's diagram, `diagram-design` | under the change |
| the change in the whole | none | the atlas's map with the changed parts marked, `diagram-design` | under the change |
| a data model | a box drawing | an entity diagram, `diagram-design` | a subsystem's journey |
| states | a box drawing | a state chart, `diagram-design`, the start `verify-formally`'s check offered after it | a subsystem's journey |
| a decision's options | a shape diff | the decision's diagram, `diagram-design` | under the change |
| a plan | a file tree | the plan's diagram, `diagram-design` | under the planning change |
| a concept | pseudocode | an explanatory figure, `anatomy` | under the change |
| the interface | none | the captures of the interface check | under the change |
| the repository | a file tree | the map and its pages, `architecture-map` and the `explain` start | the atlas |

The table is a menu, never a limit: on the owner's ask, make what fits the shape, another kind included.

# Drawing a picture in text

This page is how show-me draws a box picture in the reply: boxes, lines and arrows made of text characters, which read the same on every surface that shows the reply in a fixed-width font. Read it when a reply would draw boxes and arrows rather than one of `SKILL.md`'s text views; whether to draw, and in which form, is the table of the turn and the shape on [method.md](method.md).

## Pick the kind from what you show

| What the reply shows | Draw |
| --- | --- |
| steps and the decisions between them | a flow |
| a whole and its parts | a tree |
| a stack of levels, each using the one below | layers |
| messages between parts, in time order | a sequence |
| states and the events that move between them | a state chart |
| things and how they connect | a relationship picture |
| before and after, or options side by side | a comparison |
| a loop whose output feeds its input | a cycle |
| a choice along two axes | a matrix |
| events in order | a timeline |
| a type with its fields and methods | a class box |
| components and the wiring between them | a component picture |
| what runs where | a deployment |
| who does what with the system | a use case picture |

## Keep it within the bounds

- At most 72 columns on every line, so a narrow pane, a terminal and a PR body show it unwrapped.
- At most twelve nodes. A larger subject splits inline into an overview of its parts and one picture per part, each beside the sentence it explains, only while each part keeps these caps; where a part would not, draw the part that decides and never past them: past the caps stands method.md's one offer, and a lasting visual is the owner's ask.
- Every label is the name the code uses: the function, the file, the state, the table, the endpoint. Never paraphrase a name; when a label is too long for its box, widen the box and narrow its neighbours.
- Keep labels short around the names: a long label breaks the alignment of every line it crosses.

J-147 S4 settles split against offer: a larger subject splits inline only while each part keeps the caps, else it is offered. J-175 S1 (the register's rows of 2026-11-05, "The keeper over the oracle" and "The seven cuts"; the 0.2.0 series on Codex): past the caps the part that decides is drawn, and nothing is offered. J-204 S1 (the register's row of 2026-11-08): past the caps the one offer of method.md stands.

## Give each weight one meaning

- Heavy or double lines for the one part the reader should watch.
- Single lines for the structure.
- Dashed lines for what is optional, asynchronous or removed.

A weight that means nothing is decoration: stars, nested frames and emphasis on every box hide the point, so leave them out.

## Draw the arrows so they read

- One arrowhead style in a picture: `──►` and `▼`, or `->` and `v` in plain ASCII.
- Flow runs left to right or top to bottom; an edge that goes back is routed around the outside, never across the picture.
- Lines do not cross. When two would, move a node or split the picture in two.
- Label an edge only when it means something its target does not already say.

## The forms

Each form is the smallest that shows its kind: take its shape and give it the code's names.

A flow with a decision:

```text
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────────┐ yes ┌────────────┐
│ readSave │───►│ isUnchanged? │────►│ cachedFile │
└──────────┘    └──────┬───────┘     └────────────┘
                       │ no
                       ▼
                ┌────────────┐
                │ writeFile  │
                └────────────┘
```

Layers:

```text
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ routes/     http handlers   │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ services/   the domain      │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ store/      the database    │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

A sequence:

```text
 client           api             db
   │  POST /save   │               │
   │──────────────►│  INSERT       │
   │               │──────────────►│
   │               │◄──────────────│
   │◄──────────────│               │
   │  201          │               │
```

A state chart, its one back edge routed around the outside:

```text
┌───────┐ submit ┌─────────┐ approve ┌──────────┐
│ draft │───────►│ pending │────────►│ approved │
└───────┘        └────┬────┘         └──────────┘
    ▲                 │ reject
    └─────────────────┘
```

A class box and its relation:

```text
┌───────────────┐ 1     * ┌─────────────────┐
│ User          │─────────│ Order           │
├───────────────┤         ├─────────────────┤
│ id: int       │         │ id: int         │
│ email: string │         │ total: number   │
├───────────────┤         ├─────────────────┤
│ login(): bool │         │ total(): number │
└───────────────┘         └─────────────────┘
```

A deployment, the asynchronous edge dashed:

```text
          ┌───────────────┐
          │ load balancer │
          └───────┬───────┘
          ┌───────┴───────┐
          ▼               ▼
     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
     │ web-1   │     │ web-2   │
     └────┬────┘     └────┬────┘
```

The other kinds keep the same parts: a tree is the shallow file tree of `SKILL.md`; a component picture is the deployment's boxes and lines, one box per component; a comparison is two boxes side by side whose rows line up; a cycle is a flow whose last arrow returns around the outside; a matrix is a table; a timeline is one vertical line with a `├──` entry per event; a use case picture is the actors on the left and the system's box with its actions inside.

## Check it before you send it

- Draw it in a fenced `text` block, so it keeps its fixed-width font, right after the sentence it explains.
- Count the widest line: 72 columns at most. Close every box and line up every column.
- Read it once as the owner would, without the code beside it: does it answer the question the sentence raised? If it does not, cut it or change its kind.

# Show me: the practice's mechanics

This page holds where show-me's work lands in the workspace and the commands it runs, which `SKILL.md` names by their nouns. Read it with `SKILL.md` when the work lands in the workspace.

passages.text:
## Where its work lands

A picture or a view the owner asks to keep is drawn by a fresh agent under the change's working files, `.greenline/tmp/<id>/`, by the brief and the form `.greenline/WORK.md` gives ("Durable visuals"), and kept with `greenline picture keep <file> --change <id>`, which writes it and its manifest `<slug>.visual.json` under `.greenline/visuals/<id>/` together, the owner's words its `ask`; every other write into the change's folder of the visual home is refused. The surface's `renders` fact is the status line's `surface:` line; `greenline status` prints the running surface's row. The count reads every text picture, a box drawing by its boxes, a tree by its lines, a sequence by its lifelines and a drawing of labels joined by arrows by its labels, and a mermaid picture by its nodes; pseudocode carries no drawing glyphs and is never counted. Where the harness hands the hooks the reply's text, the next turn's status line names a picture past twelve nodes or 72 columns, `picture: one past its cap at turn <n>`; a turn that changed code and drew no shape, `picture: the turn changed <n> files and drew no shape`; a second offer in a change, `offer: a second picture offer in this change`; and an offer of a picture status names drifting, stale or deleted, `offer: the offer at turn <n> remakes <id>`; each a notice, never a refusal, and elsewhere these words hold alone. The offers are counted per change in a working file under `.greenline/tmp/sessions/`, never in the record, and no turn's end is held for a picture. Before a durable picture is drawn, its brief stands at `.greenline/tmp/<id>/pictures/<slug>.brief.md`, one line each, `- question:`, `- form:`, `- nodes:`, `- finish:` (text, branded SVG or interactive), `- palette:` and `- reader:`; `greenline picture keep` reads it into the manifest's `brief`, refuses one that does not read, and `greenline status` names a kept picture without one (GL0606).
passages.reason: show-me's mechanics since J-110 S4: an accepted picture made into the change's folder of the visual home with its manifest by the work guide's brief, and the surface's renders fact on the status line; since J-134 S1 the hook's line for a rubric turn that carried neither a picture nor an offer. J-147 S3: the offer memory in the record and the index, and the two holds with their kinds. J-175 S1 (the register's rows of 2026-11-05, "The keeper over the oracle" and "The seven cuts"; the 0.2.0 series on Codex): the offers' memory, the picture owed at a turn and the turn's end holds leave, since J-176 S1 removed them; a kept picture goes through greenline picture keep. J-204 S1 (the register's row of 2026-11-08, "One offer per change at the caps"): the count reads every text form, the turn's end names a code-moving turn that drew no shape, a second offer and a remake offer, and the brief's file and its notice.
